answer_1.quote: Specifically, we introduce a model capable of directly generating fluent spoken audio captions of images without the need for natural language text

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the I2S system, we can use any method that measures the semantic information contained in the generated speech. We consider two sets of end-to-end metrics: word-based and retrieval-based, and one set of proxy unit-based metrics. ... such as BLEU-4 (adjusted ngram precision), METEOR (uni-gram F-score considering word-to-word alignment), ROUGE (n-gram recall), CIDEr (TF-IDF weighted n-gram cosine similarity), and SPICE (F-score of semantic propositions in scene graphs).

answer_4.quote: we asked AMT workers to transcribe into words a set of 500 captions generated by our I2U→U2S system and also evaluated their naturalness. Three workers transcribed and three workers rated each caption, allowing us to compute an MOS score
answer_4.guideline: Workers transcribed spoken captions and rated naturalness on a scale from 1 to 5 (MOS).
